findings.title: Timeout races leave actor submissions running through cleanup deadline
findings.scenario: No inclusion after resume or resume failure. Parent Promise.race reaches absolute campaign deadline minus10s, but each actual wallet send may still be in its default540-second confirmation wait started after proving. Parent then attempts receipt collection and actor.close awaits that same busy application promise. Supervisor kills pending cleanup instead of cleanly settling the writer. No cancellation is caused by Promise.race.
findings.repair: Configure an actual bounded confirmation lifecycle for each started submission within parent absolute deadline, leaving time for both canonical reads and cleanup; ensure every submission promise settles before disposal. Do not detach pending writer work. Use existing supported wait configuration/guard boundaries rather than a second send loop.

findings.title: Read-only collection lacks per-operation deadline reserve
findings.scenario: Collection starts with10s remaining; journal canonical receipt reads can each take20s and ctx.node.getTxEffect is unbounded. First stalled actor can consume all remaining campaign time so second available receipt is never attempted, despite pure collector test passing.
findings.repair: Reserve enough time before waiting finishes; apply explicit remaining-time bounds to each actor receipt/effect read and save available/unknown evidence without replacing original errors. Bound original read continuations so no late evidence writes race cleanup.
findings.regression: Real existing wait/actor composition with a stalled confirmation/read must settle before cleanup deadline and still attempt/preserve the other available actor outcome. Synthetic collector immediate errors alone do not prove this boundary.
